newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Metals - Aluminium, copper premiums fall.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Metals - Aluminium, copper premiums fall.

text.p: Taipei base metal traders said on Tuesday that Taiwan's spot copper and aluminium premiums had been trending lower in recent trading days due to a seasonal lull in demand.
Taiwan's spot aluminium premiums have fallen to US$90-95 per tonne over LME cash prices, down from $90-105 two weeks ago.
Traders said the market was slowing because many buyers already have covered their third-quarter demand through long-term supply contracts.
"The aluminium market is very quiet now," said a U.S. metal trader in Taipei. "We offered at $95 premium a tonne, but no one wanted to buy."
Taiwan's third quarter aluminium import premiums were settled in early June at US$90-95 per tonne over LME futures' prices, up from US$84-89 per tonne in the second quarter.

Taiwan copper import premiums were at $55-60 per tonne over LME cash prices, down from $57-62 per tonne two weeks ago as buying interest remained sluggish during the recent copper futures rally, metal traders said.
"Copper premiums are falling, because buyers have been sidelined in the recent (futures) bull run," a metal trader said.
Traders said local copper wire and strip prices went the opposite direction, rising to reflect anticipation of a further rally in world copper futures prices.
"Local copper product prices are still rising as many traders expect to see a further rally in copper futures," a trader said.
